content.user_title: Improve Your LinkedIn Profile for the Right Audience
content.value_statement: LinkedIn profiles can lose interested visitors when headlines, About sections, and Featured items do not address their needs. This skill reviews each section in reading order and rewrites weak content while preserving what works.
actual_capabilities: Ask whether visitors arrive from posts, search, introductions, or shared profile links before suggesting changes.
Review headlines for clear work descriptions and a relevant reason to visit the profile.
Rewrite the first two About lines to identify the audience and the outcome.
Structure the remaining About section around audience, outcomes, checkable proof, and a next step.
Recommend up to three Featured items and prioritize the strongest resource.
Identify effective sections to preserve and explain why they work.
limitations: Does not promise LinkedIn search placement, follower growth, or response rates.
Does not include LinkedIn scraping, account access, or automatic profile editing.
Needs supplied profile text, audience context, and checkable evidence for specific recommendations.
VoiceMOAT voice tools require a separate connection; the source states that the connector requires a Pro or Enterprise plan.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Consulting Offer
use_cases.description: Help consultants explain whom they serve, what changes for clients, and which Featured resource supports the offer.

use_cases.title: Align a Profile With Published Posts
use_cases.description: Help professional creators make their headline and About section reflect the subjects visitors already recognize from their posts.

use_cases.title: Update a Profile After a Role Change
use_cases.description: Help professionals explain a new role to visitors arriving through introductions while keeping existing proof and effective sections.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Profile Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my LinkedIn headline and About section: [text]. Ask how visitors find me, then identify the section most in need of revision.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a Headline
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite my headline: [headline]. I help [audience] with [problem]. Visitors arrive from [source]. Keep it clear and avoid keyword lists.

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild the About Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite my About section: [text]. Use [audience], [outcome], and [verified proof]. Start with two direct lines and end with [next step].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: structure a complete About section using supplied evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Full Visitor Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [headline], [About], and [Featured items] for [audience] arriving from [source]. Rank changes, choose three Featured items, and explain what to preserve.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate section priorities without unnecessary rewrites.

output_examples.input: My headline is Operations Consultant. I help small manufacturers reduce scheduling delays. Most visitors arrive from my production planning posts.
output: Suggested headline: I help small manufacturers reduce production scheduling delays.
This headline identifies your audience and the problem your posts address.
Preserve any About evidence that supports this specific work.

output_examples.input: I advise small clinics on appointment workflows. My client approved a case study showing shorter booking times. My Featured section lists five resources.
output: Suggested About opening: I help small clinics improve appointment booking workflows. My work focuses on reducing booking delays.
Follow with the approved case study, including only results you can verify.
Feature the case study first, then select two resources that support the same audience.
Keep the existing client evidence if it is accurate and approved for public use.

best_practices: Provide current section text and identify the main visitor source before requesting a rewrite.
Use checkable results and obtain permission before naming clients or sharing their work.
Review suggested changes in your own voice and keep sections that already serve the intended audience.
anti_patterns: Packing the headline with keywords or disconnected job titles.
Inventing results, client endorsements, or promises of search placement.
Rewriting every section without identifying which parts already work.

faq.question: What parts of my LinkedIn profile does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews the headline, the opening and remaining About text, and Featured items in the order visitors encounter them.

faq.question: What should I provide for a useful review?
faq.answer: Provide your current section text, intended audience, main visitor source, and evidence you can share publicly.

faq.question: Will it improve my LinkedIn search ranking?
faq.answer: It does not promise search placement. It focuses on clear writing for people who visit your profile.

faq.question: Will it change my LinkedIn account automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides review guidance and suggested text, not account access or automatic publishing.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: No. The core review uses your supplied text. Optional VoiceMOAT tools add voice context when connected.

faq.question: Will it rewrite every section?
faq.answer: No. It identifies effective sections to preserve and concentrates changes on content that does not serve your audience.
